title: Adic realization for systems of Frobenius coefficient morphisms
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and the coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with
$A_n=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ and $k_E=A_1$. Let $X_0$ be a separated
finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $\Phi$ the $q$-power scheme
Frobenius, $g_\gamma$ the geometric-Frobenius automorphism and
$\kappa^{(m)}:L\Phi^{m*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_\gamma^{m*}$ the comparison of
[prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison].

Let $K_\bullet=(K_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a normalized $A_\bullet$-system of
[def-trf-adic-system], $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$, with normalization
isomorphisms $\nu_n:K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$; no
Weil structure is assumed. A *compatible system of Frobenius coefficient
morphisms* on $K_\bullet$ is a family of Frobenius coefficient morphisms
$\psi_n:L\Phi^*K_n\to K_n$ of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism]
such that
$$
\nu_n\circ(\psi_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n)=\psi_n\circ L\Phi^*(\nu_n)\circ\mu_n
\qquad(n\geq1),
$$
where $\mu_n:(L\Phi^*K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}
L\Phi^*(K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n)$ is the monoidality of pullback
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]); no invertibility is assumed.
Examples: the scheme-Frobenius maps $\varphi_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$ of a system
with a strict Weil structure at every level, and the systems
$\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$ of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model],
item (2), attached to a lattice $K_{\mathcal O}$ and a clearing of
denominators $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$.

Put, for a geometric point $\bar y$ of $X$,
$$
P_n=R\Gamma_c(X,K_n),\qquad P_{\bar y,n}=(K_n)_{\bar y},\qquad
P_{\mathcal O}=R\!\varprojlim_nP_n,\qquad
P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}=R\!\varprojlim_nP_{\bar y,n},
$$
the derived limits of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] of the towers
in $D(\mathcal O_E)$ (via the point identification of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]) whose transition maps are the
composites $P_{n+1}\to P_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n$ of
item (1) below, with projections $\mathrm{pr}_n$. If $K_\bullet$ is the
reduction tower $K_n=K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ of an integral
object $K_{\mathcal O}$ ([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]), then
$P_{\mathcal O}=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ by
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and
$P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}=L\bar y^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K_{\mathcal O}=:K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$
is the completed stalk of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

Call a family $f_\bullet=(f_n)$ of endomorphisms $f_n$ of $P_n$
*compatible* if $f_n$ corresponds to $f_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n$ under
the isomorphisms of item (1), and call an endomorphism $V$ of $P_{\mathcal O}$
in $D(\mathcal O_E)$ a *lift* of $f_\bullet$ if
$\pi_n\circ(V\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n)=f_n\circ\pi_n$ for all $n$, where
$\pi_n:P_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n\to P_n$ is the
$A_n$-linear map adjoint to $\mathrm{pr}_n$; likewise for the stalks. Then:

1. *Levelwise perfectness and normalization.* Each $P_n$ and $P_{\bar y,n}$ lies
in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_n)$, and $\nu_n$ induces isomorphisms
$P_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n$ and
$P_{\bar y,n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{\bar y,n}$.
1. *Integral realization and lifts.* $P_{\mathcal O}$ and
$P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}$ are represented by bounded complexes of finite free
$\mathcal O_E$-modules, and every $\pi_n$ is an isomorphism. Every
compatible family of endomorphisms has a lift, and every $V$ with
$\mathrm{pr}_n\circ V=f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_n$ for all $n$ (for instance the
derived limit of a morphism of towers) is a lift of $f_\bullet$.
1. *Compatibility of the Frobenius operators.* For every $m\geq1$ the global
operators $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)=T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})$ of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] form a compatible family on
$(P_n)$, and for $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point $\bar y$
the stalk endomorphisms $\psi_{n,m,\bar y}=(\psi_{n,m})_{\bar y}\circ\iota_{K_n}$
(normalized as in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]) form a
compatible family on $(P_{\bar y,n})$.
1. *Traces.* If $V$ lifts the compatible family $f_\bullet$, then the
categorical trace $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V\mid P_{\mathcal O})$
reduces modulo $\varpi^n$ to $\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(f_n\mid P_n)$ for
every $n$; hence
$$
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V\mid P_{\mathcal O})
=\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(f_n\mid P_n)\bigr)_n\in\varprojlim_nA_n=\mathcal O_E,
$$
independently of the lift. In particular the elements
$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi_\bullet)\mid P_{\mathcal O}\bigr)$
and
$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(\psi_{\bullet,m,\bar y}\mid P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}\bigr)$,
the traces of any lifts of the families of item (3), are well defined.

Here $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}$ is the categorical trace of
[def-trf-categorical-trace] formed over the commutative ring
$\mathcal O_E$, with the duality data of [lem-trf-chain-supertrace].

proof.text: Levelwise perfectness and normalization, clause (1). Apply [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness] to each $K_n$: both $P_n$ and $P_{\bar y,n}$ have bounded finite cohomology. We establish perfectness below rather than identifying finite cohomology with perfectness over $A_n$. For compact support use [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] with $f=a_X$, $A=A_{n+1}$, $B=A_n$, then apply $R\Gamma_c(X,\nu_n)$. Since $R\Gamma_c=\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Ra_{X!}$ with $\operatorname{Fib}_s=\Gamma(s,-)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and $Ra_{X!}K_{n+1}$ is bounded, [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction] for $t=s$ moves the reduction through $\operatorname{Fib}_s$. This gives $P_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\simeq P_n$, naturally and compatibly with successive reductions. For an arbitrary geometric point use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] on its ringed-topos pullback: apply its tensor comparison to $K_{n+1}$ and the constant $A_n$-module, whose pullback is again the constant $A_n$-module, then compose with $(\nu_n)_{\bar y}$. The K-flat change-of-rings construction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies the resulting object $L\bar y^*K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n$ of $D(\bar y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$, and [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction] for $t=\bar y$, applied to the bounded $L\bar y^*K_{n+1}$, identifies its sections with $P_{\bar y,n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n$ in $D(A_n)$. Thus $P_{\bar y,n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\simeq P_{\bar y,n}$. This argument does not require the geometric point to be a finite-type morphism.

source.place: Proof (1); stalk tensor comparison on arbitrary ringed topoi

proof.text: Integral realization, first part of clause (2). Write $O=\mathcal O_E$ and $t=\varpi$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $O$ is local; by clause (2) of [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules], applied to the finite $O$-module $O$, $O\simeq\varprojlim_n O/t^n$. For either tower $Q_n=P_n$ or $Q_n=P_{\bar y,n}$, step 1 supplies exactly the normalization hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-rlim-perfect-complete], and $Q_1$ is perfect for the following elementary reason. The DVR statement identifies $A_1=O/(t)$ as a field. Represent $Q_1$ by a complex $C$ of $A_1$-vector spaces; choose complements $Z^i=B^i\oplus H^i$ and $C^i=Z^i\oplus L^i$, where $Z^i=\ker d^i$ and $B^i=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$. The restriction $d^i:L^i\xrightarrow{\sim}B^{i+1}$ makes the $L^i\to B^{i+1}$ summands contractible, leaving the zero-differential complex $(H^i)_i$. Its terms are finite-dimensional and vanish outside a finite interval by step 1; choosing bases makes it bounded finite free. Apply that theorem with $A=O$, $I=(t)$. It gives a perfect realization $Q=R\varprojlim Q_n$ and canonical isomorphisms $\pi_n:Q\otimes_O^L A_n\simeq Q_n$ compatible with the projections and transitions. Choose a bounded finite-projective representative of $Q$ using [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Every one of its terms is finite free: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] at the maximal ideal of $O$; the supplied $f$ is a unit, so localization changes neither the ring nor the module. Denote the resulting bounded finite-free complex by $M$. Its quotients $M_n=M/t^nM$ compute $Q\otimes_O^L A_n$ by [lem-pc-kflat-closure] and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so via $\pi_n$ they represent the given tower and its projection maps. In particular all $Q_n$ are perfect, completing the levelwise perfectness assertion without any ambiguity in the notation $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}$.

Lifting chain representatives, clause (2). Transport a compatible family $f_n$ through $\pi_n$ to endomorphisms of $M_n$ in $D(A_n)$. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], these are chain maps modulo chain homotopy. Choose a representative $g_1$. Inductively, choose any representative $g'_{n+1}$ of $f_{n+1}$. Compatibility implies that its reduction $r(g'_{n+1})$ is homotopic to $g_n$, so $r(g'_{n+1})-g_n=dh_n+h_nd$ for maps $h_n^i:M_n^i\to M_n^{i-1}$. In fixed finite bases, lift every entry of $h_n$ along the surjection $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, obtaining $h'_{n+1}$. Set $g_{n+1}=g'_{n+1}-(dh'_{n+1}+h'_{n+1}d)$. Since $d^2=0$, this is a chain map homotopic to $g'_{n+1}$, still representing $f_{n+1}$, and its reduction is exactly $g_n$. This proves the induction with strictly compatible representatives; it assumes neither invertibility nor a strict tower morphism as input.

Pass the matrices of the $g_n$ to the limit. Each $M^i$ is finite free and only finitely many terms are nonzero. Clause (2) of [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_O(M^i,M^i)$ with the inverse limit of its quotient Hom modules. Hence the compatible matrices define maps $g^i:M^i\to M^i$. The equations $dg_n=g_nd$ hold modulo every $t^n$; separatedness of the finite free modules, supplied by the same clause, gives $dg=gd$. Thus $g$ is a chain endomorphism of $M$ whose reduction is $g_n$ for every $n$. Conjugating its class by $M\simeq Q$ produces a lift of $f_\bullet$. Apply this construction separately to the compact-support tower and to each stalk tower.

source.place: Proof (2), Lifts, inverse limit of the corrected chain maps

proof.text: Projection criterion, last part of clause (2). Let $V$ satisfy $\mathrm{pr}_nV=f_n\mathrm{pr}_n$. Represent $V$ on $M$ by a chain map $v$, using [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], and represent the transported $f_n$ by a chain map $a_n$ on $M_n$. The projection is represented by the quotient $q_n:M\to M_n$ by step 2. Apply the injectivity assertion of that same cited bijection, now over $O$ with source $M$ and target the restricted complex $M_n$: there is an $O$-linear chain homotopy between $q_nv$ and $a_nq_n$. Since $t^nM_n=0$, each component of this homotopy factors uniquely through $M/t^nM=M_n$. The factored homotopy proves $v\bmod t^n\simeq a_n$ as $A_n$-linear chain maps. Consequently $\pi_n(V\otimes_O^L A_n)=f_n\pi_n$. This also proves the assertion for any endomorphism furnished by a morphism of towers; uniqueness of the lift is not claimed.

source.place: Proof (2), final projection/adjunction assertion, proved on the free model

proof.text:
Compatibility of iterates in clause (3). Let $r_n=-\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n$. The given equation is compatibility for $m=1$. For the induction step use $\psi_m=\psi\circ L\Phi^*(\psi_{m-1})\circ c$, the recursion of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], where $c$ is the pullback composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Finite reduction commutes with pullback by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; its composition coherence is [fix-prop-coherence]. Apply $r_n$ to the recursive composite and insert $
u_n$ and the pullback reduction comparisons. Naturality moves $
u_n$ past the pulled-back factor, the induction hypothesis replaces $r_n(\psi_{n+1,m-1})$ by $\psi_{n,m-1}$, and the given compatibility replaces $r_n(\psi_{n+1})$ by $\psi_n$. Composition coherence identifies the remaining comparison with that for $\Phi^m$. More explicitly, write $\mu_{n,m}:r_nL\Phi^{m*}\xrightarrow{\sim}L\Phi^{m*}r_n$ for the reduction comparison. The induction gives the typed equation $
u_n\circ r_n(\psi_{n+1,m})=\psi_{n,m}\circ L\Phi^{m*}(
u_n)\circ\mu_{n,m}$: after inserting the recursive expressions on both sides, naturality and composition coherence reduce it to the given equation at $m=1$ composed with $L\Phi^*$ of the equation at $m-1$. This is the asserted compatibility for every positive $m$.

Global operators, clause (3). Put $h=\Phi^m$, proper by [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism]. The formula of [prop-trf-graph-operator] is $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)=R\Gamma_c(X,\psi_{n,m})\circ b_{h,A_n,K_n}$. Apply [lem-trf-proper-compact-unit-reduction] with $A=A_{n+1}$, $B=A_n$ and $K=K_{n+1}$. Its displayed identity reduces the first arrow $b_h$ to $b_h$ at $rK_{n+1}$. Naturality in $K$ then transports it along $
u_n:rK_{n+1}\simeq K_n$. For the second arrow, whose source $Lh^*K_{n+1}$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}$ by clause (i) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability], naturality of the compact-support coefficient comparison [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] and its point-sections realization [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction] identifies its reduction with $R\Gamma_c$ of the reduced coefficient map. Step 6 gives exactly $
u_n\,r(\psi_{n+1,m})=\psi_{n,m}Lh^*(
u_n)\mu_{h,K_{n+1}}$. Composing these two identities gives $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)$ under the normalization of step 1. This proves compatibility of the global family for every $m\geq1$.

source.place: Proof (3), global-operator compatibility; proper-graph unit route retained from the returned split

proof.text: Stalk operators, clause (3). For $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, the Stalk normalization paragraph of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] supplies $\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$ and identifies the operator at each finite level as $(\psi_{n,m})_{\bar y}\circ\iota_{K_n}$, without a lattice or Weil hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-fixed-stalk-identification-reduction] with $h=\Phi^m$, $A=A_{n+1}$, $B=A_n$ and $K=K_{n+1}$. Its displayed identity identifies the reduction of $\iota_{K_{n+1}}$ with $\iota_{rK_{n+1}}$ under the stalk coefficient comparisons. Naturality transports this identification along $\nu_n$ to $\iota_{K_n}$. The same natural comparisons send the reduction of $(\psi_{n+1,m})_{\bar y}$ to $(\psi_{n,m})_{\bar y}$ by step 6. Reduction preserves composition, so the reduced composite is $(\psi_{n,m})_{\bar y}\circ\iota_{K_n}$ under the stalk normalization of step 1. Thus the stalk operators form a compatible family.

source.place: Proof (3), last sentence, fixed-stalk identification and reduction of its composite with the coefficient map

proof.text: Traces, clause (4). Represent an arbitrary lift $V$ by a chain endomorphism $v$ on the bounded finite-free model $M$, using [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative]. The formula of [lem-trf-chain-supertrace], valid over every commutative ring, gives $\operatorname{tr}_O(V)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(v^i)$. Reducing a matrix reduces its diagonal sum, so modulo $t^n$ this is $\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(v^i\bmod t^n)$, the categorical trace of $V\otimes_O^LA_n$ on $M_n$, by the same formula. Since $V$ is a lift, $\pi_n$ conjugates this endomorphism to $f_n$; conjugacy invariance, clause (1) of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] at the finite coefficient ring $A_n$, gives the required residue $\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(f_n\mid Q_n)$. Clause (2) of [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules] for $O$ identifies $O$ with $\varprojlim A_n$, so these residues determine the integral trace uniquely, independently of the lift. Steps 3–4 supply lifts of the families in step 7, hence their global and stalk traces are well defined.

source.place: Proof (4), supertrace and uniqueness from all residues

proof.text: The reduction-tower identifications in the statement. Let $K_n=K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ with its canonical $\nu_n$. By [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] for $f=a_X$, $Ra_{X!}K_{\mathcal O}=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRa_{X!,n}K_n$, the derived limit of [def-weil-derived-limit] with its Roos triangle, and $R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}K_{\mathcal O})=\Gamma(s,Ra_{X!}K_{\mathcal O})$ by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The functor $\Gamma(s,-)$ is exact on complexes [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], so it carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles, and it carries the termwise product of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] to the termwise product, since sections of a product sheaf are the product of the sections. Hence it carries that Roos triangle to a Roos triangle of the tower $(P_n)$ regarded in $D(\mathcal O_E)$; its transition maps are $\Gamma(s,-)$ of $Ra_{X!}$ applied to the reductions $K_{n+1}\to K_n$, which are adjoint to $\nu_n$ and thus equal the transition maps of the statement. So $R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ is a derived limit $P_{\mathcal O}$. For the stalk, [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] with $g=\bar y$ defines $L\bar y^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K_{\mathcal O}$ as the derived limit of the tower whose $n$-th term is $L\bar y_n^*K_n$, with the reduction transitions; applying $\Gamma(\bar y,-)$ in the same way gives a derived limit of $(P_{\bar y,n})$. Only exactness and preservation of products of the sections functor are used, so this step is elementary.

split_report.blueprint: Steps 1, 2–5, 6, 7–8, 9 realize source clauses (1), (2), iterate part of (3), global/stalk part of (3), and (4), respectively. Step 10 retains the reduction-tower identifications. The two extracted nodes make precise the coefficient compatibility arguments hidden in source proof (3) and the returned step 7; the proper-graph route is unchanged.

tool_uses.why: The valuation ring is local, needed to specialize finite-projective local freeness; this is a coefficient-ring tool.
Clause (2) supplies completeness, separatedness, and the Hom inverse-limit bijection for finite O_E-modules, used for the chain matrices and trace residues.
The exact Stacks 09AW algebraic perfect-tower theorem is explicitly the route named in unit step (ii); it gives realization and canonical reductions at a point.
Generic local algebra converts the finite-projective terms of the perfect realization into finite free terms; at the local maximal ideal its localization is trivial.
Bounded free models are K-flat, allowing ordinary quotient complexes to compute derived scalar extension.
Generic derived change of coefficient rings identifies the K-flat quotient model and the stalk coefficient comparison in the correct coefficient category.
Stacks 064B identifies derived maps from bounded projective complexes with chain maps modulo homotopy, needed for the explicit lifting and projection arguments.
Generic monoidality for arbitrary ringed-topos pullback supplies the stalk comparison without a finite-type hypothesis on the geometric point.
The termwise pullback composition isomorphism is the comparison in the iterate recursion and fixed-stalk normalization.
Generic finite-coefficient comparisons preserve the units and counits entering the graph operator; the trace unit has no separate coefficient-unit lemma.
Generic composition and exchange coherence ensures that the reduction comparisons preserve the iterate and proper graph comparisons.

Step 8 takes its chain supertrace formula over an arbitrary commutative ring (O_E and A_n); unit sk-p-trace, which the adic unit does not cite, is the only place this trace computation is stated; the blueprint proof (4) cites it.
Step 8 takes conjugacy invariance (clause 1) of the categorical trace at A_n, as the blueprint proof (4) does; it is stated only in unit sk-p-trace.
Natural finite reduction through geometric-point sections, used for both normalization and operator compatibility.
Exactness of sections at an algebraically closed point, used with its elementary preservation of products to identify the Roos triangles.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NW-28178c3dd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against main-20261015 and found one small citation gap, now fixed. The item statement matches the main-20261015 source exactly after whitespace normalisation. The delivery repairs a human return by replacing the long old step 7 with steps 7 (global operator) and 8 (stalk operator) and adding two statement-only nodes; every step is now under 2,000 characters. Both new nodes are true, typed correctly, strictly smaller than the item and not clauses of it. They hold in the small cases I tested: h=id, a point X, K=0 and N=j. lem-trf-proper-compact-unit-reduction says reduction preserves the unit / Rh_*=Rh_! arrow of prop-trf-graph-operator for any proper h. lem-trf-fixed-stalk-identification-reduction says reduction preserves the fixed-point stalk identification iota. I checked that neither is a duplicate: thm-trf-finite-coefficient-map covers only strict Weil complexes, and lem-trf-global-operator-naturality, lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility and the Zariski tensor-composition coherence nodes are other statements. I recomposed steps 7 and 8 from the two nodes, the naturality of beta/sigma and of b/iota, and step 6's typed equation; both are correct. The coefficient category is pro-étale with constant (A_n)_X throughout.
